title: Flames shoot from Kuromanta during an excavation in a thunderstorm

tellings.quote: They look back up and all of a sudden there's flames shooting out of the top of the mountain.

plain: During a dig at Kuromanta, a mountain in Akita, Japan, that some people call a pyramid, a thunderstorm broke out and the diggers looked up to see "flames shooting out of the top of the mountain." Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who has his own theory about what pyramids were built for, tells this from a book on the excavation written by a man named Suzuki. Drumm gives no date for the book or the dig, and he tells it as a sign that the mountain works like a machine powered by energy.
